A blockchain-based system with a uniform structure can facilitate secure communication between different computers. By incorporating a food supply chain as an example, we will explore how such a structure can be utilized. To achieve this, we will demonstrate the feasibility of applying these components within a blockchain-based system, including a centralised execution of contracts. Additionally, we will present a custom architecture featuring a block explorer that visualises the block content and a dashboard displaying the system's operational status. To optimise storage and processing capabilities, we will rely on oracles and data compression techniques, while ensuring the security of the system through time-based authentication of the contracts.

Generative models have become a standard approach for creating synthetic cell shapes, helping to formulate hypotheses about cellular development. In this study, a new method called iCell is developed, utilizing implicit representations and neural networks. By integrating supervised adversarial training with maximum likelihood and minimum energy loss, iCell produces structurally accurate and varied cell shapes. Additionally, iCell is capable of modeling the probability distribution of actual cell shapes and generating new cells. A method for creating multi-compartmental cells based on cortical cytoskeleton arrangements is also presented. Finally, iCell's application in estimating the probability of network configurations given cortical actin arrangements demonstrates its practical value in guiding experimental design and interpreting observations.

Blind individuals typically rely on screen readers to navigate documents, utilizing a series of keyboard shortcuts to move through text sequentially. However, a significant portion of disabilities includes print impairment, which hinders an individual's ability to read text. Notably, screen readers are incompatible with color and image representation, rendering them ineffective for color-coded documents, charts, graphs, and other visually informative resources. Consequently, a conventional screen reader experience falls short in addressing the needs of color-blind individuals. To bridge this gap, our research aims to enhance the accessibility of screen readers by identifying areas where color information is crucial and implementing novel keyboard interactions to make this information readily available. To this end, our study involves gathering and analyzing a substantial dataset of a student's coursework, which utilizes color to convey critical information. This analysis reveals that a substantial number of assignments employ color for data differentiation and categorization. Following an investigation into the feasibility of detecting color-based structure in a document, a proposal for describing interactive elements is developed. Ultimately, an exploration of potential challenges and limitations is identified, including data that is not yet representable in an interactive format.

Pre-trained language models based on the Transformer architecture have significantly enhanced performance in various NLP tasks. However, due to the self-attention's inherent nature, certain pretraining objectives are incompatible with generalization, and others leveraging masked tokens are also flawed in this context. This issue is rectified by XLNet, a new model trained using an autoregressive objective, which achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple tasks and datasets, including multiple-choice tasks and major benchmarks of NLP.

We've analyzed how stellar activity affects the transmission spectra collected at low resolution during transit spectroscopy and demonstrated that such activity can be effectively mitigated using simultaneous high-resolution observations. This has been illustrated through transit spectroscopy simulations of two hypothetical planets, focusing on atmospheric water and the impact of a high-convection envelope on transit spectra. These simulations were conducted assuming a stellar activity level of 10^4 in activity spots and showed that water absorption features in the spectra of a planet with a radius of 2.5 R⊕ could be confused with a convective envelope on a convective star. However, such a convective envelope is unlikely to be detected in a star with a convective envelope due to noise, but could potentially be mistaken for a convective star if not properly accounted for. Moreover, our study showed that accounting for uniform limb brightening patterns at low resolution and uniform limb rotation patterns at high resolution significantly reduces the impact of these convective envelopes. These results highlight the importance of accounting for and accounting for uniform limb brightening patterns and uniform limb rotation patterns when interpreting transit spectroscopy data.

We will explicitly construct conformal metrics with constant curvature on Riemann surfaces featuring singularities using ODE derived from a type of meromorphic 1-forms. This approach will have an application in classifying a type of metric with constant curvature on the 2-sphere, specifically those with two conical singularities, which arises from studying the conformal block diagram for \((2,2,2)\).

Research into the swimming motion of the centipede forficatus near the surface of water-water interface shows that it uses an unique strategy that differs from fully submerged swimming. This strategy is distinguished by the centipede's ability to leverage surface tension to produce an efficient propulsive force. In the fully submerged scenario, a damped version of the classic Stokes flow is applicable, and when partially on the surface, a nearly incompressible flow assumption applies. Numerical simulations indicate a transition in the centipede's swimming mechanism occurs at a critical value of its mass-to-weight ratio, and as the centipede's mass increases, its maximum swimming speed decreases. This is attributed to a shift in the balance between the centipede's weight and the propulsive force it generates.

The speed and trajectory of a tsunami generated from a cosmic impact depend on variable factors such as crater formation, liquid behavior, particle interactions, and wave propagation speed. Utilizing the adaptive mesh refinement technique with a high-resolution, adaptive code, this study examines the growth and dynamics of a tsunami in a spherical basin filled with diverse materials at different compressibility levels. By refining the mesh to capture the largest tsunami waves more accurately, this research demonstrates improved simulation outcomes compared to uniform-grid models with a similar number of grid points. The findings also indicate that grid refinement strategies can yield similar results regardless of whether the most grid points are positioned towards the basin's center or edge.

Recent observations of large galaxies in the early universe were made difficult to explain due to their unexpectedly high star formation rates. To study the origin of a specific subset of large galaxies at high redshifts, a new dataset of 1711 galaxies was collected using the JWST NIRCam. This dataset focused on 176 massive galaxies at high redshifts that were previously unidentified in the optical or NIR bands. It was found that the new dataset could accurately detect the starlight of these galaxies in the 2-micron to 5-micron wavelength range with high confidence. Notably, a large proportion of these galaxies were detected at higher luminosities than their counterparts in the zBUD sample, indicating the existence of a large population of galaxies that were previously unidentified. This dataset revealed a large number of galaxies that were obscured by dust in the optical and NIR bands, which was consistent with the existence of a large population of dusty galaxies in the early universe. The findings suggest that the existence of a large population of dusty galaxies at high redshifts may be necessary to reconcile observational data with theoretical models of galaxy formation and evolution.

By incorporating two topological terms into the Einstein-Hilbert action, we create a novel seven-dimensional theory of gravity. The resulting field equations are highly non-linear and complex in form. When further broken down using our proposed formalism, the equations simplify and reduce to four-dimensional Einstein equations with a specific cosmological constant under certain conditions. A key feature of our gravity model is its ability to incorporate a primary field that links seven-dimensional geometry to its ten-dimensional supergravity and seven-dimensional M-theory counterparts, thereby providing insight into the internal structure of four-dimensional spacetime. Additionally, our analysis reveals that these topological terms do not influence particle behavior in local calculations but may play a crucial role in understanding the global properties of spacetime, as evidenced by the modified black-hole solution that we derive.

In a long and narrow container with horizontal axis, two types of disks with varying sizes and weights are arranged: a regular sequence where all disks of one type are followed by a single disk of the other type, and an alternating sequence where these two types of disks alternate.  We have calculated the pressure for both configurations using an exact method in the limit of a large number of disks, and found that our theoretical results match very well with perfectly simulated jammed configurations. Moreover, our findings have been compared to real jammed configurations, both simulated and experimental.  We found that our theoretical pressure can accurately reproduce the main features of packing and pressure in experimental realizations, including a maximum in pressure when the disk size ratio and size difference are comparable.  Moreover, our theoretical pressure matches the dynamic measurements of pressure in real systems.

Research has shown that while the effects of El Ni\~no/La Ni\~na variability on global precipitation patterns are interconnected, their impacts differ significantly. Focusing on the relationship between seasonal precipitation patterns and phase-locked variability in the context of the HadGEM2-ES model, our study reveals that precipitation responses vary greatly across regions. We observe that precipitation differences between high values are more pronounced, indicating a greater sensitivity of regions with high seasonal precipitation to certain phases of variability. This sensitivity is driven by the difference amplification effect, where precipitation responses to certain phases of variability are enhanced by the interaction of mean precipitation levels and phase-specific perturbations. This phenomenon underscores the complexity of modeling and predicting precipitation patterns in the context of climate variability.

When materials like glasses undergo deformation, various scales of motion occur simultaneously. At the atomic level, a phenomenon known as non-affine expansion occurs. This process becomes more pronounced the more the material yields. However, measuring non-affine deformation directly poses significant challenges due to its transient nature and the materials' behavior. To study this deformation, researchers proposed an optical technique that employs polarized white light. This method employs incident and scattered polarized light to detect changes in polarizability and density fluctuations, which are indicative of non-affine deformation. Using this method, researchers were able to quantify the non-affine deformation in materials and distinguish it from an alternative explanation related to stress-induced linear anisotropy. Furthermore, researchers observed that the non-affine deformation accelerates significantly as the material approaches yielding, particularly near the yield point, where there is a nearly exponential increase. This newly developed method holds promise for correlating the non-affine deformation with phenomena such as strain softening and mechanical properties in other systems.

This research aims to develop a comprehensive, low-dimensional model that takes into consideration the effects of aging and environmental pollution on a population. To achieve this, we apply the Euler-Lagrange principle, enabling us to derive an existence theorem for statistically balanced states and a fundamental result on the stability of these states. Additionally, our model is further refined by factoring in the influence of psychological factors, resulting in the derivation of key dynamic properties and, ultimately, proving a fundamental result using a classic method of Lyapunov. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our mathematical approach.

The researchers develop an extended version of hypersequential substructural logic by expanding the underlying algebraic structures. To ensure the validity of the decidability result, they restrict the expansion to a specific contraction property. Building on existing work in sublogical communities, they enhance the hypersemantics approach and then apply the matrix completion method to prove the decidability of the resulting logic class. By examining individual cases, the team evaluates the computational complexity of verification, inconsistency testing, and other key subproblems, while also exploring links to existing contraction property results in hyperstructural frameworks.

Hierarchical taxonomies, like categories of products or tasks, have numerous applications.
However, maintaining and enhancing these hierarchical classifications proves to be difficult.
Existing taxonomy enrichment techniques, which often draw from co-occurrence-based relationships, tend to overlook the natural nested structure within taxonomies.
Alternatively, recent research has applied tree-structured representation learning, yet it fails to take advantage of the inherent hyperbolic properties in data.
Our proposed method, HyperExpan, utilizes a hyperbolic neural network to learn a more natural task and subtask representation in the form of a hyperbolic tree.
By integrating hyperbolic geometry properties, HyperExpan seamlessly integrates this representation into training a hyperbolic neural classification model, allowing task instances to automatically fill into the classification hierarchy.
Our manual review and user studies demonstrate that HyperExpan is more effective than existing methods in expanding and classifying task instances accurately, particularly at the lower levels of the classification hierarchy, and generate human-readable fillings accurately.

This research explores how electric fields impact non-covalent bonds in molecular dimers, specifically focusing on the behavior of H-bonds and van der Waals complexes. To examine this, we build upon existing theories, expanding their applicability to complex scenarios where multiple interactions occur within a time frame. Our findings indicate that as the intensity of the electric field increases, the behavior of molecules deviates from non-polar behavior, while the impact of the electric field varies depending on the type of intermolecular bond involved. Additionally, we demonstrate that our time-averaging approach accurately replicates quantum chemical simulation results, and it reveals that polar molecules respond more significantly to electric fields, resulting in a greater reduction in intermolecular forces.

The growing importance of Industry 4.0 has led to a surge in research on advanced production scheduling techniques to manage the increased complexity brought about by novel technological advancements and non-traditional uncertainty types. A crucial element in these technologies involves adaptable machine tools, and accurately assessing the uncertainty associated with these resources is a significant area of investigation. Existing approaches often treat uncertainty as fixed and time-independent, and are limited in their scope to a specific set of pre-determined error categories. In contrast, a different type of uncertainty, known as non-deterministic uncertainty, is characterized by its freedom from statistical laws, resistance to a specific parameterization, and unchangeability, even with more data available. A network-based model recently developed in this field addresses these limitations by considering all possible error categories and assigning weights to each, which are determined through an optimization process guided by empirical data. To overcome the limitations of current methods, we propose a novel approach to assessing non-deterministic uncertainty weights in the context of automated scheduling for Industry 4.0 resources, which involves learning weights based on historical unit processing times and using an optimization process guided unit routes to minimize a loss function and maximize the robustness of scheduling. This method has been tested on a network of 10 nodes, effectively outperforming conventional uncertainty models established in literature in terms of robustness and at significantly reduced computational costs, thus enabling real-time applications.

Cyber-Physical Systems require robust resilience properties to withstand disruptions and recover operational capabilities promptly. To address this challenge, a framework has been developed that utilizes Signal Temporal Logic to specify and verify resilience properties, focusing on the restoration of a system's safety or safety-related subsystem. Furthermore, this framework incorporates a cost function to evaluate the cost of disruptions and system recovery. By relying on linear optimization techniques, a safety recovery path can be computed and verified for compliance with resilience properties. The framework's utility is demonstrated through numerical examples representing diverse resilience scenarios.

One of the most pressing enigmas in modern cosmology and particle physics is the existence of dark matter. A variety of experiments have been successfully implemented to detect dark matter particles interacting through both weak and gravitational forces. A network of precise accelerometers can serve as a sensitive indicator of dark matter interactions. We examine the potential of accelerometers to identify dark matter over existing search techniques and consider the optimal configuration for accelerometers in a network to maximize their sensitivity. By comparing their potential to that of cold gas experiments, we analyze the implications of different interaction strengths between dark matter particles and ordinary matter. By adhering to existing constraints, it may be possible for a network of accelerometers to increase the range of interaction strengths probed, contributing to the search for dark matter.

This study derives a sharp long-term gradient estimate for the solution to a nonlinear diffusion equation on a complete weighted Sturm-Liouville gradient estimate. The obtained estimate generalizes previous results from Souplet-Zhang and Zhou, extending them to a broader class of nonlinear diffusion equations with non-negative and non-constant diffusion coefficients. As an application, we establish global and local Liouville theorems for superharmonic functions on complete weighted manifolds. Furthermore, we provide new gradient estimates for a nonlinear heat equation on complete manifolds with non-positive Ricci curvature.

Radio sources powered by an active accretion process at the core of galaxies are crucial components of the universe's radio emission, yet many other faint radio sources, which are significantly more abundant, lack a thorough understanding. We conducted an analysis of a comprehensive sample of approximately 1,200 compact, faint radio sources at redshifts below 0.3, which have flux densities ranging from 0.1 to 1 Jy and angular sizes of 1-5 arcsec, by examining their ANTS characteristics. Our study employed a stacking technique that enabled us to examine subtle source sub-structures below the IWF threshold. We discovered that a considerable portion of our source sample, which is approximately 30%, lacks any form of asymmetry, which is further supported by the absence of detectable jet-like features. Our ANTS analysis reveals that compact, faint radio sources exhibit T-type values close to 1000, which indicates that they are likely composed of free-free synchrotron radiation, which is distinct from the sources that are more extended in nature. We also observed that compact, faint radio sources lack any correlation between their radio luminosity and redshift fluctuations, which is consistent with the steady-state model. Our source sample lacks any correlation between their jet fraction and luminosity, which is consistent with the expectation that luminous sources are more likely to possess jets.

Hidden Markov Models are a widely recognized information flow safety guarantee. They have been previously defined using information states, which, in a probabilistic setting, take the form of probability distributions over algebraic distributions. Our contribution is to provide a more abstract characterization of HMMs that is independent of probabilistic distributions. This new definition relies on the notion of monads and showcases a connection between HMMs and Zippermaps - distributed storage systems that safeguard quantitative information flow. By establishing the equivalence between our new definition and the original HMMs based on information states, we validate this more abstract perspective. Furthermore, we demonstrate that HMMs address both nonleakage and delay attacks, and we establish a correspondence with probabilistic simulations, which is a more general information flow safety guarantee.

We develop a class of stochastic advection problems at large scales in which the field being studied changes significantly over time due to the presence of coherent structures in the background flow. Our work involves analyzing coherent structures' effects in two ways: first, through a deterministic approach where their impact is tied solely to how often the field is observed relative to how quickly these structures change; second, by incorporating uncertainty in both the field's initial state and the positions of these structures, based on statistical probability distributions. This second method accounts for additional sources of non-locality and time asymmetry that were previously overlooked. As a result, our study reveals that accurate predictions of complex phenomena, such as the evolution of electromagnetic fields in the atmosphere or ocean, require not only an accurate representation of coherent structures but also precise initial conditions on their positions and sizes.

We maintain that many "good" fits for elastic scattering data are driven by
overly restrictive optical model parameterizations rather than the actual
underlying physics. In contrast, we suggest that adopting pheno models based on
effective physical mechanisms provides accurate fits and meaningful
interpretations. For example, using the Wound Distribution Model yields successful
fits for a variety of systems and adds a useful perspective to the Wound Number
Wentzel-Wilmer (WWWA) framework. In addition, effective disintegration mechanisms
enhance our understanding of Coulomb interference in the Coulomb Nuclear interference
Effect (CNE) region.

A general approach to describing the thermal properties of the radiation field's equation of state has been developed for the first time within the framework of a canonical ensemble model's heat bath system. When considering the influence of Casimir's effect on the thermal properties of blackbody radiation, the pressure and heat capacity have shown a significant influence under the conditions of the meandering geometry of the cavity. When the scale of thermal fluctuations becomes comparable to the cavity size, the thermal properties exhibit considerable deviations from standard blackbody radiation predictions. These deviations are further analyzed in the context of a canonical ensemble model's heat bath system with thermal fluctuations.

Protecting users of location-based services with significant privacy requirements is extremely difficult when multiple specific locations are shared within a short time frame due to the significant interdependence of these locations. Unfortunately, most existing research and product solutions primarily consider the privacy of individual, isolated locations, rather than user location trajectories. Our work aims to bridge this gap by introducing a time-based privacy model tailored to safeguarding user location trajectories. This model incorporates conditional prior distributions to capture the interdependence of locations over time. Furthermore, it can be computed efficiently as a tractable average related to single-time frame privacy metrics. Our proposed solution involves two mechanisms: the first being a straightforward method to ensure any trajectory's privacy by limiting the probability distribution. The second being a more advanced mechanism that optimizes the probability distribution to minimize the resulting penalty. Our research also involves conducting comprehensive experiments using real-world data to evaluate the performance of our solutions and their potential applications.

A novel point cloud representation called Normal Distribution Transform (NDT) was pioneered to replace LiDAR point clouds in robot localisation, offering improved performance in computational efficiency and accuracy, as demonstrated in real-world scenarios with complex objects and patterns. The traditional point cloud localisation methods, such as Iterative Closest Point (ICP) and Normal Distribution Transform-Transformer (NDTt), leverage the properties of NDT and Transformers for optimal performance. However, due to the constraints of NDT-based point cloud fitting, NDTt falls short of its potential. To overcome this limitation, a new point cloud localisation framework, NDT-Transformer, is proposed, which directly applies the Self-Attention mechanism to the probabilistic map and target NDT without the need for point correspondence or an optimisation step. The framework achieves superior performance with a reduced parameter count and a lower F1-score at optimal conditions, showcasing a more straightforward and efficient approach compared to the point cloud localisation's state-of-the-art methods.

Research using resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) has shown promising results, but its reproducibility and reliability are still uncertain. This study aimed to identify key factors contributing to the variability of rsFC in multisite studies, and determine the optimal settings for collecting, preprocessing, processing, and analyzing rsFC data. A comprehensive investigation was conducted using a large dataset of 1,240 healthy individuals across 26 sites, utilizing various imaging, labeling, and analysis techniques. Notably, our findings revealed that using a two-step search strategy significantly improved the reproducibility of rsFC, with up to 90% correlation, by testing new methods in previously unseen data. Additionally, our results suggest that using task-based functional MRI data, task-anatomical MRI co-registration, and a large sample size can substantially reduce rsFC variability, with sample size accounting for 60% of between-subject FC variance and 75% of test-retest reliability. A, priori modeling and prediction accuracy analysis also identified collection and preprocessing quality, sample size, and task-based functional co-registration as critical for modeling rsFC accurately, with effect sizes of 0.38, 0.43, and 0.26, respectively. By pinpointing the factors contributing to rsFC variability and identifying the most effective methods for collecting and processing rsFC data, this study provides valuable guidelines for the design of future rsFC studies and highlights the need for task-based functional co-registration,

In the study of name games within beeping networks, two entities communicate by transmitting short beeps without the capability to detect silence, and a message is conveyed only if one entity transmits while the other remains silent. While traditionally, transmitting messages requires multiple phases to confirm the presence of another entity, and then sending a message a linear number of times, the authors propose a more efficient approach called adaptive naming, where each phase adapts to the behavior of other entities. By only sending messages when it's certain that the other entity is listening, adaptive naming reduces energy consumption. The authors establish a lower bound on the number of phases, proving that adaptive naming requires at least $n/2$ phases, and present an adaptive naming algorithm with $n/2 + O(1)$ expected phases. The study also explores the scenario with faulty entities that may not transmit as scheduled, and derives the corresponding lower and upper bounds on the number of phases.

Recent advancements in NLP for code-mixed texts have been limited by a lack of high-quality datasets, especially for real-world applications such as spoken CM texts. Switching Point CM Dataset presents a solution by introducing a new framework for reencoding text at sentence boundaries, enabling the effective processing of CM speech texts through a contrastive task. A six-language dataset featuring 300 hours of speech data is also presented, along with its characteristics and a comparison with other CM speech datasets available today. Experiments conducted on sentiment and language switching classification tasks demonstrate that sentence-level reencoding proves to be a robust method for handling multilingual speech CM texts in a relatively straightforward manner.

Using a combination of density functional theory and time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory, we've analyzed the critical temperature and isotope effect in H3S, a hydrogen-rich superconductor, across various pressures. Our density functional theory calculations, using the quasiparticle self-consistent GW method, enabled us to account for electron-phonon interactions and gained. We then determined the presence of a van Hove singularity at different energy levels and its impact on the superconducting properties of H3S. We found that as pressure increases, the superconducting behavior undergoes significant changes due to the shifting positions of phonon and van Hove singularities, ultimately influencing the material's critical temperature.

This paper proposes a novel method to introduce spatial constraints for navigation in dynamic environments. Our proposed corridor map can segment an environment into distinct zones: navigable areas, non-navigable areas, and uncertain areas. Our spatial constraint generation approach can be seamlessly integrated with any motion planning algorithm as a pre-processing step, where the uncertainty zones on the corridor map are translated into barycentric coordinate constraints that can be directly applied to motion planners. We present both analytical and experimental evaluations demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, which consistently outperforms or matches the performance of common local navigation strategies like cost fields and vector fields while yielding better results than basic motion planning techniques.

This paper introduces a visual localisation method based on a surfel-based map. The proposed method combines learned features and 3D scene information to facilitate re-localisation. Unlike traditional approaches, our approach leverages 3D geometric information without 3D localisation and can be easily integrated with any point cloud extraction and rendering pipeline. Our method employs a learning-based descriptor to match 3D geometric features and achieves efficient and accurate visual re-localisation using 3D trackpoints and surfel renderings. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach can accurately re-localise sequences with and without IMU and texture, and achieves comparable performance to other methods.

In the context of multiuser MIMO, the task of jointly selecting users and precoding can be reformulated as recovering a group-sparse signal from limited observations. This problem can be addressed using the Group LASSO approach, which, as demonstrated, converges to the optimal solution of the original problem at each iteration. Furthermore, the iterative algorithm enhances the group-spectral efficiency compared to the orthogonal training and precoding method and achieves near-optimality with the minimum effort of the group LASSO approach.

We demonstrate that the rational function semifield of a tropical curve has a finite set of generators over a specific semifield. This involves identifying a particular finite set that generates the semifield. We also provide evidence from various cases, including discrete and genus-zero tropical curves, which satisfy this property. Moreover, we show that the tropical curve in question possesses a divisor of a certain type, which enables the generation of the semifield. To establish this result, we developed a finite set of tropical functions that satisfy certain criteria, which involves solving a linear system and verifying a property over the semifield.

This note primarily focuses on measuring the speed of a conditioned process approaching its quasi-stationary equilibrium under specific assumptions regarding its distribution. In reverse, we establish that a conditioned process nearing its quasi-stationary equilibrium in distribution implies a specific functional condition. Under distinct hypotheses, we demonstrate convergence towards this state. Notably, one set of assumptions align with a specific model, while another with a different one. Our approach builds upon a conceptual framework introduced by Doukhan, Genton, and Sapsford in 2017. Examples provided include the continuous-time Markov chain system described by Bressan et al. in 2020.

We've demonstrated that combining the Fox-Hatcher generators with the 3-node Vassiliev generator and setting their values to 0, 1, and 2 respectively, provides a valid assignment over the Kauffman variable over all 3-valent oriented graphs.

The connection between unconventional superconductivity and NEMATIC order is of
utmost importance in the analysis of cuprates and iron-based superconductors.
A challenge arises, however, as experiments have not conclusively identified
evidence of nematic order, particularly in the case of LiFeAs, where
fluctuations are predicted to be relatively weak. A notable prediction,
suggested by recent theoretical studies, is that nematic order in LiFeAs should
manifest at temperatures around 10 Kelvin, which is below its superconducting
critical temperature. A thorough examination of NEMATIC order parameters in LiFeAs
using first-principles methods, including advanced treatments of electron-phonon
interactions, has revealed no substantial evidence of such order. Furthermore,
calculations indicate that the nematic susceptibility in LiFeAs is about a factor
of 10 smaller than in iron-based superconductors that demonstrate clear
evidence of nematic order, such as FeSe monolayer.

This research reviews a global analysis of Type-II two Higgs doublet models and considers how upcoming measurements of the SM-like Higgs and Z boson decays at future colliders will constrain the model's non-decoupling parameters. Based on current constraints, the fit allows for a small range of values for the cosine of the Higgs mixing angle and a certain range for the Higgs-VBF coupling ratio, in addition to a limited domain for the Higgs coupling to WW and ZZ relative to its standard model counterpart. Accuracies of one percent for the Higgs coupling ratio are anticipated from the measurement of the Z boson decay width at future colliders, such as ILC and FCC-ee. By comparing these measurements with those of the Higgs coupling to W, Z, and Z bosons, researchers expect to set a 0.066 constraint on the Higgs mixing angle, which, in turn, will be used in conjunction with other constraints, primarily from electroweak precision tests and B-physics, primarily the B to X_s to gamma ratio, resulting in precise values for the Higgs mixing angle and the Higgs coupling to top quarks, in addition to limits on its coupling to bottom quarks. By considering these findings, researchers expect to anticipate a one percent accuracy on the Higgs coupling to top quarks and a five percent accuracy on the Higgs coupling to bottom quarks at the 2σ level.

We demonstrate through simulated molecular learning, using evolved neural networks, that complex self-assembly processes can be discovered autonomously, even in scenarios with complex, dynamic environments. By eliminating direct guidance or reward functions, our approach allows for entirely decentralized and autonomous synthesis of desired materials. Notably, our method, which draws inspiration from natural selection rather than biological evolution, can adapt to and solve a wide range of unrelated problems, including those where traditional energy minimization techniques are ineffective. Moreover, our approach yields valuable insights into the characteristics of useful material patterns, ultimately enabling a deeper understanding of the principles governing self-assembly and providing guidance for designing future bottom-up fabrication protocols.

Our research centers around the notion of Strong $A$-anomalies, where an anomaly arises in a a-a-c-triangle diagram, even if the a-a-invariant amplitude remains undetermined. We demonstrate that a Strong A-anomaly in a chiral gauge theory leads to an irreconcilable contradiction between gauge theory unitarity and the gauge principle. We also explore the possibility of embedding fermions with non-trivial representations in nonchiral gauge theories. Additionally, a novel type of chiral gauge theory, the $SO(10)$-Witten model, is introduced. This theory exhibits Stueckelberg massless mechanisms, intricate connections with the Witten effect, and potentially rich phases influenced by quantum gravity, making it a highly intriguing object for various theoretical and mathematical studies.

This study examines the stationary Navier-Stokes equations on a d-dimensional space with periodic boundary conditions and a given L^2-based Besov space initial velocity, where the initial exponent can be greater than or equal to the spatial dimension. We demonstrate two key findings. Firstly, when the initial exponent is strictly less than odd numbers, there exists a critical threshold for the initial velocity's regularity such that any arbitrary norm in those smaller regularity conditions results in local well-posedness for the given equations. This is an extension of a prior discovery made by Cantarini, Guerber, and Keraudren in their analysis of the heat equation, where they found that data regularity such that 0 < gamma less than (d-1)/2 results in a critical threshold for the initial velocity's regularity such that any arbitrary norm in those smaller regularity conditions results in uniform boundedness for the solution flow. This implies weak well-posedness of the solution. Secondly, when the initial exponent is greater than or equal to the spatial dimension, we find counterexamples in which even arbitrarily small and smooth initial velocities become arbitrarily large within a very short period of time, thus showing that the problem is ill-posed in those conditions. This implies that data regularity such that (d-1)/2 less than or equal to gamma results in ill-posedness. A significant aspect of our work is its extension to cases where d is at least 4, thus generalizing previous works

We are studying how the interactions between magnons impact the behavior of magnon modes in antiferromagnetic insulators. Our analysis reveals that the interaction between two magnon modes leads to a non-linear shift in their frequencies and enhances the thermal generation of magnons with opposite spin orientations. As a result, one mode becomes dominated by magnons with a specific spin direction, creating a phenomenon known as thermal magnon squeezing. This interaction also influences the absorption spectrum in a specific frequency range, causing a non-linear shift in the absorption spectrum. Our findings are supported by the observations made in the neutron scattering experiments, indicating that the interaction between two magnons significantly affects the properties of magnon modes and the absorption spectrum.

This research introduces two modifications to Loidreau's code-based cryptosystem with the aim of enhancing its security and efficiency. Firstly, we propose replacing the initial component of Loidreau's scheme with its simplified version, making the system more suitable for implementation and while overcoming a potential vulnerability. Then, in an effort to boost security, we suggest applying a permutation linear transformation over the rings $\mathbb{F}_2[u]/(u^2)$ and $\mathbb{F}_{2^r}[u]/(u^2)$ to the plaintext matrix in Loidreau's encryption, instead of the conventional approach of performing matrix multiplication. We've demonstrated the advantages of this novel method over existing solutions.

To improve pre-trained language models (PLMs), which are trained on large datasets using methods like masked language modeling, researchers are exploring new strategies. One limitation of these models, however, is that they cannot capture word meanings beyond their basic units. To overcome this issue, we introduce Dict-BERT, which incorporates a comprehensive dictionary of compound words and phrases derived from word embeddings and a pre-existing phrase dictionary. By doing this, we enable more effective training and better language understanding in our PLMs. Experimental results show that Dict-BERT significantly outperforms other models, particularly in tasks involving languages like German. To facilitate further research, our Dict-BERT model is being made publicly available.

The minimum weight spanning tree in graphs and its higher-dimensional complex counterparts have been extensively researched. They are related to the persistent homology diagram via the Bottorendal-Spudich-minimal acycle mapping. This paper examines this mapping for various random simplicial complex models and proves that the expected number of non-Bottorendal-Spudich-minimal acycles grows linearly with the model's size parameter, while the maximum weight difference and the maximum degree also grow linearly. Furthermore, the paper applies its findings to the Wedin-Clifford simplicial complex model and constructs a persistent homology diagram for a minimum weight spanning acycle, demonstrating that the wedging height of any simplex is bounded by its homological rank.

This study reveals vulnerabilities in vertical federated learning (VFL) to a specific privacy breach, even when employing encryption techniques. A novel attack method, called a multi-client linear program (MCLP), is introduced that allows an adversary to successfully breach a user's local data in VFL's hierarchical structure. The developed solution addresses challenges that make the attack scalable and efficient, surpassing existing research in HFL. Furthermore, the attack's success has been validated mathematically and empirically in both synthetic and real-world scenarios. Interestingly, increasing model complexity, data samples, or security encryption methods can only slightly mitigate the attack's effectiveness, and even secure multi-party computation techniques can be bypassed. As a countermeasure, the paper also explores how incorporating regularisation techniques can prevent data leakage in VFL.

A theoretical framework called B-Meson Dark Baryon Higgs Model is proposed to explain certain phenomena observed in particle collisions, specifically those involving proton-antiproton collisions. Utilizing the light-cone sum rules method, a non-perturbative calculation is performed to determine the probability of a specific type of particle decay, which results in a measure known as the decay constant. This decay constant provides insight into the strength of the interaction between the involved particles. Calculations are carried out for multiple values of a variable called dark anti-Baryon mass, specifically 0.85 to 0.95 GeV. These calculations are then compared with theoretical constraints, particularly those arising from decays that occur when a B meson interacts with a proton. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of subatomic phenomena, which is a crucial area of study within the field of particle physics.

In a Smart City environment, security forces can be viewed as dynamic resources that effectively counter cyber threats and physical attacks. We introduce the Smart City Defense Game, a model that allows for the management of security forces as adaptability resources to deal with unpredictable socio-cyber-physical attacks. Our analysis focuses on identifying the optimal distribution of security forces to ensure the health of the smart city remains intact in the face of adversarial attacks. We establish existence and convergence properties for optimal security strategies in general Markov Games, and provide a method for computing these strategies in smart city settings. Additionally, we provide evidence through simulation that the proposed security strategy exhibits greater adaptability and robustness to attacks compared to existing alternatives.

Researchers have found that the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström black holes can be
thermodynamically stable in a cavity with fixed pressure, exhibiting a single or double
Hawking-Penrose phase transition, respectively. Notably, the charged black hole's phase
transition is more intricate, involving not only BPn and RN phases, but also introducing the
charged de Sitter spacetimes, denoted as DnR, as a novel third solution. The interaction between
these phases can result in up to three Hawking-Penrose transitions, showcasing a complex
phase diagram, particularly in the charged de Sitter spacetimes. This led to an in-depth
investigation of the charged black holes' phase diagram, encompassing DnR phases, and a
comprehensive comparison with the Schwarzschild black holes' behavior. The presence of charge
reveals a more complex dependence on temperature, particularly in terms of critical points,
and a detailed analysis of these behaviors has been presented within the phase diagram's
context. Ultimately, charged black holes exhibit a more complex thermodynamic behavior,
characterized by a more complex phase diagram, and an in-depth understanding of these
phenomena has been achieved through a phase diagram analysis.

In most long-text information retrieval tasks, such as multi-document reading comprehension, we typically create a ranking of documents based on their relevance to a specific query. However, existing document ranking methods are often hindered by large dataset sizes and the issue of label noise during the training process, particularly when using pre-trained language models for model-based ranking. To address these challenges, we propose a novel training approach for the next-generation pre-trained models that incorporates bag sampling techniques to accelerate the training process and reduces the impact of label noise by using a group-wise margin-based ranking loss. To this end, a new open dataset is introduced to facilitate model-based ranking research. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach in achieving state-of-the-art performance with a significantly reduced training duration.

Recent research into graph pseudo-labeling has revealed its potential in graph classification tasks, particularly when faced with data label scarcity. Current methods rely on an all-in approach, incorporating every generated pseudo-label regardless of its quality. To address this limitation, we propose a new graph pseudo-labeling scheme called InfoPL, which selectively applies pseudo-labels based on their utility in refining the network's predictions. Our informative pseudo-labeling framework consists of two key components: the first involves graph pseudo-label generation using a selective method, and the second involves processing the pseudo-labeled graph to guide the network's learning. Comprehensive evaluations on four benchmark datasets have demonstrated InfoPL's superiority over state-of-the-art methods, with an 11.11% 1-shot performance improvement and 5.42% 3-shot performance improvement over the best existing pseudo-labeling techniques.

Betatron radiation spectroscopy may serve as both a diagnostic tool and additional detection method for the plasma accelerator developed in the AWAKE experiment at CERN's SpP. We analyzed the theoretical betatron x-ray spectrum based on two proposed plasma and laser parameters for AWAKE 2, and compared the results with the proposed detector setup, and then assessed the challenges and possibilities of using betatron emission to diagnose plasma accelerators.

The research presents the first fully verified algorithms for building distributed, private decision trees. The new methods guarantee the accuracy of the trees while meeting privacy standards. The algorithms were tested with various methods for splitting data and compared to their non-privacy versions and to models created using a distributed, private approach. The results show that the algorithms are accurate, especially when using a type of privacy that doesn't involve the exact split thresholds. The more complex splitting methods used had the least impact on accuracy for the trees. The source code for the algorithms is publicly available.

We focus on the Bregman R\'enyi divergence minimization problem in a
comprehensive, mathematical Hirschfeld-Geiss-Gir\'eath (HGG) framework,
incorporating suitable regularization techniques to address its inherent
complexity. To address this problem, we develop an iterative
optimization method, and analyze its convergence behavior by establishing key
properties that ensure its effectiveness. To demonstrate its practical
efficacy, we apply the algorithm to a specific case in data compression,
utilizing the Fisher information metric to define a distance function.

This generalises the discrete Bayesian network class to the chain event graph class, retaining the ability to conduct Bayesian inferences and maintain a consistent construction approach. BPAGs are a more comprehensive and versatile tool than discrete Bayesian networks, offering greater flexibility in modeling categorical data, which in turn affects model parameter estimation and model selection processes. In this research, a Bayesian approach to MPAG model selection is presented, employing Dirichlet priors on the BPAG's parameters. By deriving a closed-form expression for the marginal likelihood, it becomes feasible to compute the posterior distribution over BPAG models. In addition, when sample sizes are sufficient, the asymptotic properties of the model selector are investigated, revealing that it may incorrectly identify a BNPAG model when given finite sample sizes. Consequently, the methods are tested on two datasets: a criminal court case dataset and a social network dataset concerning social interactions.

In a Hilbert space, we devise a continuous, damped inertial dynamic model 
that strongly converges towards the minimum norm solution applicable to various 
well-posed optimization problems, including feasibility problems, optimization 
tasks with linear constraints and equality problems. Furthermore, we 
extensively demonstrate the applicability of this dynamic for solving 
infinite-dimensional problems with empty solutions sets, in which case it 
exhibits a rapid drift along the null space while the 
norm of the solution continuously decreases and 
asymptotically approaches zero.

This study investigates how bifurcation types, including interior bifurcations as well as bifurcations induced by changes in system parameters, are influenced by the system's noise level and other factors. Two types of bifturcations are analyzed in non-wall following mode, specifically saddle-node and saddle-node bifurcations on an invariant cycle, as well as those that occur with sufficiently high noise levels present. In wall following mode, the research shows that increasing the noise level alters the bifurcation types, specifically turning a Hopf bifurcation into a homoclinic bifurcation, and at sufficiently high noise levels results in bifurcations triggered by collisions. Moreover, the study demonstrates that in all cases, the presence of noise significantly impacts the system's critical point and its attractor shape, and, due to these changes, the robot's behavior exhibits a variety of different patterns.

Within the framework of a kinetic energy driven superconducting mechanism, the effect of impurities on the transport of quasiparticles in cuprate superconductors in the superconducting state has been investigated, employing the nodal approximation. Results indicate an inverted shape in the microwave conductivity spectrum as it varies with energy, exhibiting a peak in the conductivity at intermediate temperatures, which decreases with impurity concentration, energy, and temperature, while increasing with doping. At low energies, the microwave conductivity's behavior mirrors that observed experimentally at zero temperature, displaying a downward trend with increasing temperature. Conversely, at high energies, the conductivity's dependence on temperature reverses, increasing with temperature in the measured range due to residual carriers associated with low-lying quasiparticle excitations near the nodes, which also accounts for the observed upturn in microwave conductivity with decreasing temperature. Furthermore, the model fails to fully explain a significant upturn in microwave conductivity with decreasing temperature, which was previously proposed in literature, as well as conductivity values at zero temperature that are lower than experimentally observed values, especially at high impurity concentrations. Additionally, the model fails to account for a notable negative temperature coefficient at high frequencies in microwave measurements as well as a significant frequency dependence at low temperatures.

This passage discusses an anisotropic curvature flow, referred to as a crystalline curvature flow. A comprehensive review of this type of flow is provided, focusing primarily on the initial value problem's solvability and well-definedness.

Our proposal, GrowSpace, addresses the challenge of enabling a person to shape plants by providing precise shape guidance, specifically plant leaves, with goal shapes. To achieve this, we utilize a multi-finger haptic device to collect the desired shape from the user and employ image processing to convert leaf images into smooth, vector images. We demonstrate our approach through controlled studies in a simulated environment mimicking plant growth, showing that GrowSpace enables users to effectively shape plants. The evaluation reveals that our approach significantly improves task success rates and efficiency, with average shape acquisition time of 1.52 minutes and accuracy of 90%, compared to direct shape guidance where average time is 5.75 minutes and success rate is only 30%.

It has been established that the SLE loop measure emerges as a consequence of uniformly picking conformal maps from the product of two quantum $L$ disks. Given $\kappa\ge1$, this selection process involves maps from domains formed by welding two independent collections of quantum disks with margins $84-\kappa$ and $8+\frac{4}{\kappa}$, respectively. To support this, we have also demonstrated the conformal welding of an infinite sequence of quantum disks with constant margin 4, representing a SLE$_4$ loop. The measure for this loop measure corresponds to the length of the slices in their respective domains. Additionally, we have introduced and examined the notion of chordal SLE loop measure, which is the degeneration of the SLE loop measure when the domain converges to the upper half plane.

The Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative is a global partnership that strives for consistency in extracting biomarkers from imaging for use in psychiatry and the neurological and related disease fields. Its primary goal is to enable seamless collaboration among researchers, ensuring that their findings are reproducible and that building cumulative knowledge is feasible. A key aspect of biomarker standardisation within this initiative involves identifying and classifying image-based metrics that are influenced by variations in imaging protocols, scan quality, clinical symptoms, and medication, as well as those that are not.

We have analyzed the effects of high-spin nucleon and delta resonances on the production of kaon-lambda and kaon-sigma particles when a nucleon is irradiated. To do this, we included these new resonances in a existing amplitude to describe the process and then fitted the existing amplitude to experimental data without considering the new resonances. Our results show that the high-spin resonances can be concealed by an enhanced coupling between the existing K-N and K-Δ channels and an extra epsilon particle. Nevertheless, beyond a certain energy point (the square of the photon energy of 2.5 GeV^2), we can start to see these new resonances manifest themselves.

This research describes the process of preparing the MORPH-II dataset comprising 55,130 images. We down-sized all images to a resolution of 145 x 112 pixels. We utilized OpenCV to clean the images by applying techniques such as 3D and spherical filtering, and successfully aligned facial images with an eye-to-mouth line.

Building upon our previous research \cite{Liu:2019jxg}, we investigate the potential for Primordial Black Holes to form from density fluctuations derived from a curvaton model with a dynamically changing curvature perturbation. We employ the Fourier mode splitting approach to compute the required parameters for Primordial Black Hicles to match the Dark Matter abundance under different primordital models. Assuming the curvaton fluctuates in a sinusoidal pattern, Primordial Black Holes can produce Dark Matter when $\sigma_2=0.032$ with $k=1.3\times10^{13}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. If the curvature perturbation follows a polynomial progression, Primordial Black Holes may account for Dark Matter matter when $\sigma_2=0.011$ with $k=1.3\times10^{13}$ Mpc$^{-1}$.

University administrators and educational researchers are concerned with understanding enrollment patterns at a large scale. The size of larger institutions makes it challenging to manually examine enrollment records, so it's crucial to develop methods that can help. Our research showcases how latent variable models can be applied to map university pathways by using example courses and departments, demonstrating course prerequisites and following requirements. The model we developed can effectively extract a course hierarchy and departmental structure from course data and enable further analysis. To prove its effectiveness, we applied a mixture of models to map first-year and second-year courses at Columbia University and used the extracted structures to analyze taking certain subjects alongside university GPA.

This work focuses on the control of connected and automated vehicle (CAB) platoons.
To manage the dynamic entry into the platoon, we utilize a differential game approach,
considering two key issues: first, when to join the platoon, and second, how to adjust speed
upon joining. By formulating the entry issue as a Cursory Differential Game and the speed
adjustment as a Static Game, we establish a game-theoretic framework for analyzing these issues.
Our analysis reveals an equilibrium strategy that achieves the optimal formation control for
platoons, as well as provides insights into the impact of human-driven vehicles on the
performance of platoons. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed
approach and offer a valuable reference for future research in this area.

Otterburn and Shah [2021] developed an efficient algorithm for training logistic regression models within edge-AVC, a framework that enables asynchronous communication between servers in a data dissemination network. Their algorithm allows achievement of optimal convergence rates despite infrequent data exchange. This work continues Otterburn and Shah's research by providing a solution for parallel logistic regression training in the same framework. Achieved performance shows training can proceed without data exchange between communication-unreliable servers, solely relying on occasionally communicating a single 'anchor' server. achieved performance demonstrates the non-communication training approach is nearly as effective as the sequential approach, which demands constant communication between the anchor and the system.

The widespread dissemination of misinformation through the internet and social media significantly impacts public opinion, with generative models now capable of automatically creating deceptive news content. To detect such content, machine learning models have been developed to differentiate between real and fabricated news. Researchers focus on distinguishing between genuine and artificially generated headlines to determine their source, with available datasets used to test and refine the model's capabilities to classify unknown news. The proposed approach involves incorporating DeBERTaVante to enhance the classification of automatically generated headlines.

In polycrystalline and amorphous materials, irregularities such as stress and disorder can be used in place of the perfect crystal lattices that these materials lack. This allows researchers to create and control chemical pressure and disorder in a wide range of materials, influencing their magnetic properties. Consequently, studying these non-crystalline materials provides an opportunity to explore how charge and spin disorder interact, as well as the role of spin-orbit coupling, without needing to find a stable, disorder-tolerant crystal structure. However, there are very few materials available for this purpose, and they often come with additional complications. In this context, we examine a spin glass model with exchange frustration and chemical pressure, incorporating spin-orbit coupling, and discover through simulations that both disorder and pressure are essential in producing a chiral disordered state.

Future large-scale radio interferometers like the Low Frequency Array and the Square Kilometre Array will significantly advance our understanding of the universe. To effectively analyze the data from these massive instruments with potentially $N$ up to a few tens of thousands of antennas, the computational time required for cross-correlation calculations should be minimized. We've developed new calibration schemes where the cross-correlation calculations between all antenna pairs can be performed by utilizing the fast Fourier transform. To make this possible, the receiver channels are divided into multiple sub-bands and assigned to different processors, with the goal of optimizing the computational efficiency.

For several decades, the Markowitz framework has been the go-to approach for portfolio diversification. However, utilizing a deep learning strategy can enhance both the robustness and efficiency of modern portfolios. An novel autoencoding conditional GAN model is proposed, where the generator produces a sample from the optimized return distribution, and its corresponding input represents the return of the preceding period, enabling unsupervised learning. By having the generator mimic the true return distribution, and the discriminator differentiate between real and synthetic data, we find the Markowitz optimized portfolio distribution is non-stationary. Additionally, we prove the autoencoding conditional GAN model converges to the true data distribution, and experiments across various markets demonstrate its ability to produce more diversified and accurate distributions compared to the traditional Markowitz portfolio.

We have derived the polarized massive operator matrix element $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$
analytically in the $\overline{MS}$ scheme up to order $O(\alpha_s^3)$ for quark moments with $N \ge 5$,
considering both massless and large quark mass regimes.
This research presents the most complex and critical calculation yet in the next-to-double-next-to-leading-order analysis
for the proton side-up gluon PDF $g(x, N, \mu^2)$. Our results for the large quark mass regime
are available in numerical form and can be accessed via a publicly accessible link.

A novel Bayesian neural network approach is introduced to identify and classify gamma-ray blazars observed by Fermi-LAT, which exhibits superior performance over previous methods utilizing artificial intelligence. The current model leverages both morphological and statistical data to differentiate blazars into four categories: flat-spectrum blazar, curved-spectrum blazar, single-component model, and double-peaked model. When applied to training samples, it surpasses counterpart neural networks, offering more accurate likelihood estimates and parameter uncertainty bounds. Furthermore, it is utilized to classify a {656} Fermi-LAT blazar catalog with a comparable success rate to conventional results, yet providing enhanced classification accuracy. The results provide valuable insights for further astrophysical investigations.

This study reveals significant issues with social media content in terms of accessibility and interactivity, which are often crucial elements of the overall user experience. It's crucial to consider the limited web accessibility skills that many content creators possess. Initially, we collected real-world social media content to gauge how pervasive these accessibility problems are. The result indicates that approximately 60% of social media content violates the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG). Building on these findings, we are presenting research on practical solutions to address these issues, incorporating both successful examples and potential obstacles stemming from diverse technical platforms. By understanding the root causes of these challenges, we aim to identify opportunities for innovative web accessibility tools tailored specifically for social media content.

In this paper, we propose a new approach to defining hypergraph operations using tensors and demonstrate the equivalence of three formulations within this framework. We establish that any hypergraph can be viewed as a composition of hypergraphs formed by a common tensor-based operation. This operation allows us to calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of hypergraphs based on those of their constituent tensor parts. As an application, we define a hypergraph in terms of a specific tensor operation involving a standard basis tensor and an arbitrary vector space's set of orthonormal vectors. We then investigate the spectra of these hypergraphs. Additionally, we relate the spectra of hypergraphs to the spectra of their join. We provide explicit calculations for their adjacency and Laplacian matrices.

India achieved a groundbreaking success with the deployment and initial operations of its first space telescope, AstroSat, in 2008. The satellite has made significant contributions to multiple areas of modern high-energy astronomy, serving as a multi-messenger hub spanning from radio waves to gamma-ray bursts. Following an extensive, thorough, and comprehensive needs analysis, INSIST, a cutting-edge, versatile multi-wavelength space telescope, has been designed to meet a diverse set of research and development requirements across various fields, including astrophysics, astrophysics, research on dark energy and dark matter, astrophysics, research on exoplanets, astrobiology, planetary science, remote sensing, and other related fields. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the proposed INSIST, highlighting its unique features and capabilities.

In clinical trials for Alzheimer's and progressive diseases tracked with time-based continuous outcomes, traditional analysis techniques often assume a consistent rate of change, which may not hold true. Our research introduces a novel method using natural cubic splines to seamlessly integrate the Marshall and Olkin correlated structure into time-to-change outcomes, effectively accounting for varying rates of change without assuming a consistent rate. This approach was applied to data from the ADNI-1 and ADNI-2 trials, demonstrating its value. Results show that estimating parameters for varying rates is feasible and beneficial, and incorporating this rate variability into statistical models yields more accurate conclusions. For instance, in the ADNI-1 trial, our model revealed a notable cognitive function improvement associated with treatment, a finding that more consistent with the primary endpoint specified in the trial protocol compared to traditional models.

A novel computational approach called Action Optimization Pruning (AOP) has been developed to identify pathways between confined states in complex systems. By globalizing the action functional within Transition Path Theory, AOP efficiently reduces high-dimensional transition pathways and eliminates less significant sections, resulting in discovered pathways that closely match those found using traditional approaches like Transition State Theory and graph theory. AOP has been tested on simulated systems and biological molecules, including a three-state spin system, the folding of the chignolin protein, and conformational changes in dihydrofolate reductase, and has been shown to be capable of sampling multiple dominant pathways.

This study focuses on a parabolic variant of complex Monge-Ampere equations and incorporates an intervening term by employing the Hessian type approach of Guan-Li-Zhang. By introducing a precise L^∞ estimate and leveraging the notion of viscosity, the authors successfully prove the continuity and L^p estimate of the solution to the given Hessian type parabolic equations. Furthermore, the researchers apply their findings to a discretized Hessian type equation and derive related estimates for the discrete solution, including L^p estimates and gradient estimates in a short-term framework.

Building on Church and Turing's foundational work, numerous computational models have been developed within the context of typed lambda-calculi, each imposing various constraints to a theoretical universal computer. In contrast to these models, this research focuses on machine supersets capable of computing functions that exceed those of a universal machine. These oversized computational models are demonstrated to be effective tools for formally characterizing computational problems, particularly in the field of bioinformatics, where they have significant applications.

This concise note introduces a new approach to the conditional measure flow (CMF) equation, a type of L^1–L^∞ equation that often arises as a regularized version of the Stratonovich stochastic differential equation (SDE) when it includes irregular coefficients that lack sufficient smoothness for a classical solution, as per the De Giorgi-Nash theorem. In this context, we integrate the Stratonovich SDE with irregular coefficients into the measure space, employing a Girsanov transformation with a regularized transformation function, specifically designed to ensure its absolute continuity with respect to the flow's conditional probabilities, and then use this result to integrate the resulting Ito SDE with the regularized drift function. We establish a strong representation of the CMF in terms of an Ito SDE and provide conditions under which different regularizations of the drift function yield equivalent solutions for the CMF equation, as well as demonstrate how these regularized solutions converge to the original Stratonovich SDE in the limit as the regularization parameter approaches zero.

This research aims to investigate various types of normal structure spaces in a group G, including T_0, T_0*, T_1 and T_1*. It is demonstrated that if G has a more complex algebraic structure, the relationship between these spaces becomes well-defined. Specifically, when G is a T_0 semigroup, the spaces T_0, T_1 and T_1* become identical, whereas a more intricate group structure allows for distinct T_0* and T_1* spaces. For abelian groups, the equivalence of T_0, T_1, T_1* and T_0* holds whenever at least one such space exists. Moreover, when both G and its dual group G^ are abelian, the equivalence of T_0, T_1, T_1* and T_0* on G and T_0, T_1, T_1* on G^ respectively implies that all four spaces on G are equivalent. It should also be noted that normal structure spaces may not necessarily be disjoint unions of points in the context of group structures.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets to guide the model to extract relevant features. Furthermore, a value filling objective is introduced to help the model represent necessary meaning components during parsing, thus enabling effective handling of filling operations. To further refine the model's performance, an joint objective is proposed to concurrently optimize the auxiliary tasks and the joint SQL query generation task. Our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on Text-to-SQL datasets across domain shifting and generalization benchmarks, consistently outperforming previous methods.

In complex multi-robot environments, collision avoidance becomes a significant concern.
This study develops an innovative data-driven model predictive control (dm MPC) method to seamlessly integrate safety protocols into the navigation of multi-robot systems, thereby achieving safe path planning and real-time control under the presence of obstacles.
To tackle the inherent nonlinearity in MPC problems, the issue is reformulated as an optimization problem grounded in distribution models obtained from the collected training datasets, which simultaneously minimizes risk-sensitive costs.
Furthermore, by incorporating an online dataset updating mechanism into the MPC framework, our method efficiently accommodates the dynamic movement of obstacles, thus enabling the smooth adaptation of control actions.
Through simulation studies involving multi-robot systems, our proposed dm MPC approach has demonstrated superior performance in terms of collision avoidance and optimal control performance, exhibiting a 15% to 25% decrease in collision rates and a 5% to 10% reduction in total energy consumption compared to the traditional PID control method.

Recent data on Andromeda XXV, a distant satellite of the Andromeda galaxy, has been obtained. It consists of a compiled list of member stars, the resulting stellar velocity distribution, and resulting dynamical mass profile. Analysis revealed a constant radial velocity dispersion of approximately 4.8 km/s. The dynamical mass to light ratio at a radius of 100 pc is estimated at 100 M/$_\odot$. The best-fit mass model indicates a low central dark matter density, with a maximum of 0.022 g/cm$^3$. This is significantly lower than a recent data point for a similar dwarf galaxy of the Local Group, M32. It challenges data suggesting a high central dark matter density in dwarf galaxies. It also supports a low-metallicity, old-age, and high-inflation factor origin for field dwarf galaxies. The lower age of a similar galaxy, M32, and its higher metallicity, however, makes direct comparisons difficult.

In massive machine-type communications (mMTC), granting massive connectivity becomes feasible by employing a grant-free multiple access technique (GF-MAC) with optimized preamble sequences for low-latency uplink access in 5G-IoT. However, conventional preamble sequences have limitations, particularly in terms of higher interference and worse outcomes when the number of users is not a multiple of the frame length due to orthogonality constraints. This research proposes a novel non-orthogonal preamble design using a two-stage genetic algorithm (TSGA) that overcomes these issues in grant-free systems. The first stage generates a preliminary solution by relaxing integer constraints, while the second stage ensures optimality and feasibility. The proposed method offers up to a 15% improvement in system performance over existing approaches.

A few approaches to model the thermodynamic properties of moist air rely on approximations that can lead to inconsistencies with the first and second laws of thermodynamics. A new strategy is introduced to model moist air by thermodynamically consistent versions of these approximations, specifically, the commonly used assumptions that water vapour behaves like an ideal gas and liquid water has a constant density.

We introduce algebraic objects, which generalise ordered semirings and monoids, and extend these to objects that include elements acting as negative identities. An exterior algebra analogue is proposed, which provides a cryptomorphism for matroids, and shows that standard exterior and idempotent exterior algebras can be derived from it under specific conditions.

Research has shown that dialogue state tracking models that consider uncertainty in user input tend to outperform those that don't. However, accurately modeling the uncertainty is still a challenge. We found that the current method of using Attention BLSTM models to generate uncertainty estimates leads to suboptimal results. To improve this, we propose a new approach using Word Confusion Networks as a distributionally accurate uncertainty model, which considers the uncertainty at both the character and word levels. We tested this novel uncertainty modeling approach in both simulated and real-world environments and found it yields superior performance compared to the existing method.

We have computed Joyce's enumerative invariants for semistable coherent sheaves on smooth projective curves, focusing on rank r sheaves with l sections in generic semi-simple shape. In this situation, the moduli space of such sheaves consists of finitely many P^k's, and the associated enumerative invariants lie within the quantum cohomology of P^k, which can be interpreted as counting holomorphic sheaves on P^1. In addition, we have extended this invariants framework to other geometric settings, which include P^1 and P^2, leading to connections with existing mathematical models, specifically the macroscopic localization formula of Poon-Witten.

A critical component in simple majority voting, known as a universal collection of subsets, enables efficient computation in several group voting procedures using linear time and linear resource consumption. Determining the complexity of checking whether a given set of agents and assignments can form a universal collection is shown to be a complex P-complete task. If partial assignments are taken into account, the check becomes an NP-complete problem.

We develop a strategy for accurately estimating the degree of entanglement in a two-qubit optical system. Our proposal involves using squeezed vacuum states for one of the qubits and leveraging optimal measurement techniques to quantify entanglement.
